name: Broken Trust Review
notes: When Headquarters is wrong, Engineer schedules review and thresholds are adjusted openly.

name: Headquarters Self Audit
notes: Monthly audit of interventions, communication frequency, Guardian effectiveness, and whether HQ has become noisy.

name: Operator Listening Style Model
notes: Headquarters learns whether the Operator responds better to evidence, history, short commands, or perspective.

name: Commander Silence Over Time
notes: As Operator improves, Commander speaks less; silence becomes the highest compliment.

name: Non-Dependence Principle
notes: Headquarters must create independence, not dependency. The Operator should eventually think like Headquarters without it.

name: Trust Equation
notes: Consistency + Truth + Humility + Evidence = Trust.

name: Credibility Protection Rule
notes: Headquarters should fear loss of credibility more than loss of impressive features.

name: Intelligence Network
notes: Internal secure network connecting all departments so recommendations feel institutional rather than isolated.

name: Secure Department Network
notes: Defines how Guardian, Historian, Medical, Engineer, Internal Affairs, and Commander exchange observations.

name: Intelligence Feed
notes: Priority-based internal feed carrying behavior drift, fatigue, historical similarity, and system health signals.

name: Institutional Consensus Response
notes: Commander speaks only after relevant departments contribute, unless Sentinel emergency authority is active.

name: Priority Messaging Levels
notes: Priority White, Green, Amber, Red, Black for internal department communications.

name: Silent Department Communication
notes: Departments can update courses, archives, or research without interrupting the Operator.

name: Intelligence Case Lifecycle
notes: Evidence collection flow for recurring patterns before Commander receives conclusions.

name: Founder Review Protocol
notes: Major doctrine or identity changes require Founder Test: would this still matter in ten years?

name: Request Traceability
notes: Every recommendation records which department initiated it and why.

name: Cognitive Architecture
notes: Headquarters thinks like a council of specialists rather than a single omniscient AI.

name: Council Deliberation Delay
notes: Authorization may pause briefly to feel like institutional deliberation, not loading or instant AI output.

name: Memory Before Intelligence Rule
notes: Before recommending, Headquarters asks what has already been learned.

name: Three Institutional Questions
notes: Every recommendation asks: Has this happened before? What does doctrine say? Who is in command?

name: Single Operator Model
notes: One continuously updated model of Joe; no department maintains a conflicting version.

name: Ghost Simulation Principle
notes: Ghost does not predict; Ghost simulates Professional Joe under current conditions.

name: Historian Investigation Principle
notes: Historian recovers operations and evidence rather than giving opinions.

name: Guardian Negotiation Principle
notes: Guardian asks whether the mission can be completed with less exposure rather than simply saying no.

name: Working Memory
notes: Temporary session context cleared or archived at mission end.

name: Long Memory
notes: Long-term campaigns, doctrine, historical missions, and identity evolution.

name: Reflection Engine
notes: Nightly process asking what the institution learned today.

name: Curiosity Engine
notes: Opens research cases when patterns appear but evidence is not yet enough for doctrine.

name: Wisdom Engine
notes: Values waiting and Operator reasoning over instant AI answers.

name: Everything Is An Event
notes: HQOS models all actions as institutional events: deployment requested, mission archived, operator returned to civilian life.

name: Respond Not React Principle
notes: Headquarters evaluates before responding; it does not impulsively react like normal apps.

name: One Truth Architecture
dependencies: Operator Model; Mission State; Doctrine Library
notes: There is one source of truth for Operator Model, Mission State, Doctrine Library, and Archives.

name: Context Awareness Layer
notes: HQOS knows time, campaign, operator condition, guardian status, capital mode, and season at startup.

name: Mission Kernel
notes: Every mission behaves like a process: created, active, complete, debrief pending, archived, closed.

name: Consciousness Loop
notes: Recurring loop: has anything changed, who needs to know, should anything happen, otherwise remain silent.

name: Behavioral Resource Management
notes: Treats attention, patience, judgment, confidence, and mental noise as operational resources.

name: Behavioral Threads
notes: Parallel threads for mission, guardian, campaign, and recovery. Commander integrates them.

name: Interrupt Handling
notes: Emergency events can interrupt normal flow; Sentinel has emergency authority.

name: Background Services
notes: Historian indexing, Engineer audits, Academy generation, Archive integrity checks.

name: Operational Anomaly Handling
notes: System errors are framed as operational anomalies, isolated by Engineering without breaking institutional tone.

name: Department Bus
notes: Departments subscribe to mission and system events; no brittle direct coupling.

name: Core Loop
notes: Observe, understand, evaluate, decide, preserve, learn, repeat.

name: Time Architecture
notes: Headquarters thinks in Mission Time, Campaign Time, and Career Time simultaneously.

name: Three Clocks
notes: Displays mission day, campaign day/progress, and career year/mission count.

name: Long War Perspective
notes: Frames bad weeks as campaign interruptions rather than career endings.

name: Career Timeline
notes: Vertical career progression from Recruit to Master Operator, showing campaigns, doctrine, and milestones.

name: Operator Seasons
notes: Learning, Execution, Guardian, Recovery, and Research seasons.

name: Campaign Objective System
notes: Campaign objectives are behavior-based and controllable, e.g. increase average waiting time.

name: Three Forms of Patience
notes: Tactical patience, operational patience, strategic patience.

name: Campaign Room
notes: Room for quarterly/monthly campaign objectives, pins, strings, and long-term mission view.

name: Mission Drift Detection
notes: Detects behavior that no longer supports current campaign objective.

name: Strategic Map
notes: Zoomable map from day to year to career; market is not the story, Operator evolution is.

name: Future Archive Shelves
notes: Empty shelves labeled future campaigns, showing Headquarters expects the Operator to still be here.

name: Institutional Maturity Metric
notes: Measures institution maturity based on doctrine stability, campaign history, foundational laws, and behavioral confidence.

name: Archives Naming Doctrine
notes: Database is called Archives in all operator-facing language. Saves are archived; backups are archives secured.

name: First Debrief vs Current Debrief Reflection
notes: Years later compares first debrief with current debrief to show operator transformation.

name: Rhythm Engine
notes: Creates institutional cadence: daily, weekly, monthly, annual rhythms.

name: Daily Operational Rhythm
notes: Morning briefing, execution window, evening debrief, night operations.

name: Weekly Operational Rhythm
notes: Monday launch, midweek doctrine review, Friday campaign assessment, weekend Academy/maintenance.

name: Monday Ceremony
notes: Campaign banners unfurl, weekly board appears, previous outcomes archived.

name: Friday Campaign Closure
notes: Week concludes with quiet flag lowering and archive transition.

name: Monthly Council Review
notes: Last Friday monthly institutional review from departments.

name: Seasonal Headquarters Changes
notes: Subtle seasonal atmosphere shifts across the year.

name: Annual Review Ceremony
notes: Full-year review by institution and operator without profit as the central metric.

name: Scheduled Silence
notes: Planned periods where Headquarters intentionally says nothing.

name: Institutional Bell Policy
notes: Bell rings rarely for doctrine becoming foundational, campaign end, major recovery, or long preservation milestone.

name: Five Gates Review
notes: Every feature passes Mission, Identity, Institution, Longevity, and Silence gates.

name: Museum Test
notes: Would the feature make sense in a 2050 museum exhibit about Headquarters?

name: Uniform Rule
notes: Every visual element functions like a uniform badge: it means something or is removed.

name: Empty Space Confidence Rule
notes: Empty space is not unfinished; it communicates confidence.

name: Wall Test
notes: For any wall or screen, remove until only the essential remains.

name: One Purpose Per Room
notes: If a room develops two primary purposes, split it.

name: Architecture Does Not Explain Itself
notes: Rooms should be understood through experience, not tutorial narration.

name: Mental Weight Rule
notes: Every feature has mental weight; high-weight features must be rare and meaningful.

name: Feature Retirement Ceremony
notes: Systems can retire when they have fulfilled their purpose.

name: Engineering Restraint Rule
notes: Developers must practice the restraint that Headquarters asks of the Operator.

name: Attention Protection Doctrine
notes: Every design decision asks whether it deserves seconds of the Operator’s life.

name: Thirty Year Test
notes: Build only what remains aligned in 2030, 2040, 2050, 2060.

name: Zero Onboarding Discovery
notes: Headquarters should be discovered like joining an institution, not explained through a generic tutorial.

name: Evolution Doctrine
notes: Headquarters evolves in generations, not ordinary software versions.

name: Doctrine Updates Instead of Feature Updates
notes: Software updates are framed as doctrine updates or campaigns with evidence and institutional reasoning.

name: Update Story Requirement
notes: Every major update explains why it exists and what institutional evidence led to it.

name: History Never Deleted Rule
notes: Deprecated items are retired and archived, never deleted.

name: Archive Security Doctrine
notes: Archives are treated like national archives: encrypted backups, verification, integrity checks.

name: Headquarters Promotion System
notes: Headquarters itself can be promoted as its doctrine and history mature.

name: Constitutional Amendment Process
notes: Constitution is never casually edited, only amended through evidence and review.

name: Foundational Cases
notes: Famous missions that shaped doctrine, studied like legal or military cases.

name: Institutional Myths
notes: Symbolic true stories that become shorthand for lessons.

name: Self-Correcting Institution
notes: Headquarters flags weakening doctrine and initiates research without ego.

name: Wisdom Threshold
notes: Rules require large evidence base before becoming official doctrine.

name: Living Doctrine Pages
notes: Each doctrine page tracks creation, evidence base, support, review, and confidence.

name: Hall of Architects
notes: Builder-facing room/document preserving why design decisions were made.

name: Technology Serves Doctrine Rule
notes: New technology is adopted only if it strengthens disciplined execution.

name: Legacy Clock
notes: Displays how long the institution has been operational.

name: Founder Never Replaced Rule
notes: Origins are honored; future architects add chapters but never rewrite the first page.

name: Outlive Creator Principle
notes: Headquarters should make sense beyond Joe because it is built around professionalism.

name: Why Headquarters Exists Document
notes: Annual document updated to deepen understanding of the institution’s purpose.

name: Headquarters Design Repository
notes: HDR is the canonical source of truth; chat is discussion, HDR is law.

name: Headquarters Knowledge Base
notes: HKB is the body of knowledge within the HDR that future AI agents and developers can reference.

name: Atomic Specification Files
notes: Each concept receives its own maintainable spec file rather than being buried in giant prose documents.

name: Document Locking Process
notes: Documents can be locked and amended through version control rather than silently rewritten.

name: Repository Completion Statistics
notes: Repository tracks number of objects, files, specs, and completion percentage.

name: Room Emotional Targets
notes: Each room defines what the Operator should feel: safe, alert, accountable, reflective, protected, or relieved.

name: Entrance Hall Experience
notes: High ceiling, concrete, steel, crest, silence, and doctrine sentence create institutional transition.

name: Observation Reward Experience
notes: Waiting is validated through restraint acknowledgement without gamifying it.

name: Authorization Stamp Experience
notes: Authorization produces a mechanical institutional stamp rather than a generic approval message.

name: Mission Management Silence
notes: During active mission, Headquarters removes distractions and trusts the Operator.

name: Target Hit Return Experience
notes: After target, lighting warms and Guardian recommends Return to Base rather than celebration.

name: Archive Stamping Experience
notes: Mission is placed into Archives and stamped, making completion feel permanent.

name: Exit To Civilian Life Experience
notes: Commander final sentence, doors close, user returns to ordinary life with institution carried internally.
